tool_args.rationale: The response is smooth and saturating over the sampled input range, while changing sink gradient shifts it substantially. Fit a numerically estimated quadratic-in-input response with linear gradient and input-gradient interaction; all required predictors except u_now and s_grad are constant in the observations, so additional dependence is not identifiable.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The existing seven observations span the input and gradient ranges at the target horizon; a low-order coupled response surface can be fitted without another paid batch.
The pilot signatures suggest a bridge, but the supplied observations do not specify its state equations or expose varied horizon/state conditions needed to identify an ODE mechanistically.

considered_alternatives.option: Stefan-Boltzmann quartic or pure Newton cooling
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Neither recalled single-node law explains the strong observed gradient-dependent shift across the two open-branch measurements.
